May also be observed in STEREO A EUVI 195 on its west limb over former AR 14479, with loops over this region brightening starting around 2026-07-10T08:35Z.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is a minor eruption centered around S20E60, observed as dimming and field line movement in GOES SUVI 195 starting around 2026-07-10T07:28Z.

data.note: CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. This front is overtaken by CME: 2026-07-10T15:53Z in STEREO A COR2's field-of-view only. The source is a filament eruption near the east limb centered ~N06E63 beginning as early as 2026-07-10T12:18Z in SDO AIA 304 with the filament brightening and gradually lifting off. The filament fully lifts off around 2026-07-10T13:33Z, although the majority of the material seems to reabsorb onto the disk. The eruption is also observed as field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is also observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 after a downlink gap backfilled in. The source is AR 14485 and a C6.0 flare (S16W47) peaking at 2026-07-10T14:59Z. The eruption is also observed well in SDO AIA 171/193 as field line movement, pockets of dimming in the vicinity of the eruption, and a minor EUV wave.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, using the width in STEREO A COR2 as it appears much less wide in SOHO's field-of-view. Significant overlap with CME: 2026-07-10T13:26Z in COR2's field-of-view obscures a clear view of the leading edge for most frames.

data.note: CME observed to the NW only in SOHO LASCO C2. The CME becomes to faint to see in later imagery, and is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, or STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely a weak filament ejecta and field line movement centered ~N15W65 in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-07-10T23:15Z, in the proximity of a nearby coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D SOHO LASCO C2 only analysis using the observed source around W65 as an estimate, as such parameters could slightly vary.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and NNW in SOHO LASCO C2. The CME is seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is heavily obscured by the pylon. The source is likely a large, diffuse area of slow dimming and field line movement on the NW disk in SDO AIA 171/193, starting as early as 2026-07-11T20:30Z and centered approximately around N45W35. This source is likely also responsible for the following, overlapping CME: 2026-07-11T04:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, as the CME is blocked by the pylon in LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and also too faint to resolve in running difference imagery beyond earliest frames.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2, and NNW in SOHO LASCO C2, also NNW but heavily pylon obscured in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely a large, diffuse area of slow dimming and field line movement on the NW disk in SDO AIA 171/193, starting as early as 2026-07-11T20:30Z and centered approximately around N45W35, and may be separable with more weak field line movement to the NW in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-07-11T02:51Z but it is not too distinct. This diffuse, slow source is likely also responsible for the preceeding, overlapping CME: 2026-07-11T01:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, as the CME is partially blocked by the pylon in LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2 and W/SW GOES CCOR-1, not in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to an ongoing outage. The source of the CME is likely former Active Region 14479 or AR 14478, estimated to be located ~N17W165 and ~S05W155 at this time. There are two potential eruptive signatures observed on/around the west limb in STEREO A EUVI: one as wide field line breaking and EUV wave in EUVI 195 to the SW starting around 2026-07-11T15:05Z, and prominence movement and brightening in EUVI 304 to the NW starting around 2026-07-11T15:45Z. Of these, the SW field line movement appears to be a better fit based on timing and CME leading edge/shock appearance.

The source of the CME may likely involve former Active Region 14479 or AR 14478, estimated to be located ~N17W165 and ~S05W155 at this time, as seen in preliminary Solar Orbiter PHI imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary, very speculative leading edge measurement just relying on two frames in STEREO A COR2A and assumption of the source based on the appearance with respect to the 16:09Z CME preceding this eruption.

data.note: CME seen to the Southwest in SOHO LASCO C2 in association with a long-duration C5.9-class flare from AR 14485 (S10W68) with corresponding circular EUV wave seen best in GOES SUVI 284 imagery starting around 2026-07-12T01:00Z. This eruption is located to the South of a prominent coronal hole, resulting in this CME likely being deflected. This CME overlaps with CME: 2026-07-12T02:12Z. This subsequent CME (CME: 2026-07-12T02:12Z) appears to accelerate the Northern portion of this ongoing event (CME: 2026-07-12T02:14Z), greatly changing its morphology in later frames.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

Preliminary leading edge measurement using only the first two frames of SOHO C2 and assuming a modest 15 degrees of deflection eastward relative to the source longitude due to the presence of a coronal hole feature.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-07-12T02:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The CME is seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source of this event is a region of dimming seen located at approximately N10W45 beginning at approximately 2026-07-12T01:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 193. However, due to coronal hole proximity, this CME is likely deflected from the source location. This dimming is likely residual/expanded dimming following a C5.3 flare from Active Region 14485. This CME heavily overlaps and disturbs the morphology of CME: 2026-07-12T01:14Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the West by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-07-12T04:23Z. This event is not clearly seen by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 as it is likely far sided and obscured by the occulting disk. The source of this CME is a small eruption seen beyond the West limb by STEREO A EUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-07-12T03:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky using a longitude of W154 (STEREO A current longitude: W64) due to source location beyond the COR2A West limb and lack of SOHO/GOES imagery to triangulate.

data.note: Faint and slow CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-07-12T09:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is an M1.1 flare from Active Region 14485 (S10W68) which peaked at 2026-07-12T08:11Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Field line opening and post eruptive arcades are also seen in association with this flare in SDO AIA 171 and 193. This CME is likely deflected due to the eruption proximity to a prominent coronal hole.

The eruption is also visible in the NE quadrant of STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. A filament liftoff is also faintly seen on-disk in SDO AIA 304 imagery.

The source of this event is a very minor eruption seen along the NE limb in GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-07-13T15:45Z. Field line movement/opening is also visible in GOES SUVI 171 and 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of E90 due to source location along the NE limb and lack of visibility in COR2A to triangulate.

data.note: CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-07-13T19:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-07-13T18:53Z. The source of this event is likely far sided as no clear eruptions are visible on the disk, but field line movement is visible from beyond the SE limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-07-13T19:00Z. An estimated C9 flare is seen from preliminary Solar Orbiter STIX data, possibly from Active Region 14478, which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk around 2026-07-07. The approximate source longitude estimated from preliminary Solar Orbiter magnetogram data is S05W180.

Moving field lines are best seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the southwest in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an eruption visible from beyond the western limb likely from former Active Region 14485 (~S10W110) starting around 2026-07-15T02:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the southwest limb around this time in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery. Additionally, dimming is observed from the eruption site starting around 2026-07-15T02:55Z seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery.

There is not a good source candidate for this CME on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is possibly far-sided.

The source is possibly related to a minor eruption seen on/near the far southern limb beginning around 2026-07-15T16:24Z in GOES SUVI 304.

It is also covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. The only visible source candidate is some very minor, slow field line movement near the W limb best seen in GOES SUVI 284 as early as 2026-07-15T16:30Z.

The source of this event is minor field line movement seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 and 193 beginning at approx. 2026-07-16T06:00Z.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-07-16T10:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 due to an outage which began at 2026-07-15T20:00Z. The source of this event is an eruption from former Active Region 14485 (S10W130) beginning at approx. 2026-07-16T09:00Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 and 304. This eruption was likely slightly deflected due to coronal hole proximity.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

An opening of field lines is visible over the southwest limb in GOES SUVI 195 imagery at this time as well. This event overlaps with CME: 2026-07-17T18:00Z.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery for a few early frames before becoming too faint to observe. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, before being overtaken by brighter CME 2026-07-18T20:12Z. This CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is not clearly seen separate from the eruption resulting in CME 2026-07-18T20:12Z, but may be a brief brightening in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 near former AR 14482 starting around 2026-07-18T18:45Z, located approximately around W105-W110.

cmeAnalyses.note: This measurement is based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. This front quickly overtakes prior faint CME: 2026-07-18T19:36Z. The source of this CME is former AR 14482, observed best in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 as filament ejecta and brightening around approximately S08W105, starting around 2026-07-18T19:25Z. The eruption is observed over the West limb in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 as field line movement and the filament ejecta.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. In STEREO A COR2 imagery, however, this event is visible as a halo directed to the southeast. The source is likely a large dimming region centered near S03W35 starting around 2026-07-19T05:00Z seen in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery. Western deflection is likely due to a large coronal hole east of the eruption site.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an eruption from former Active Region 14482 (S09W120) seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-07-19T14:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: CME with an irregularly shaped leading edge first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-19T21:24Z. This CME is also seen to the W in STEREO A COR2 but disappears before leaving the FOV of STEREO A COR2. It is very faint and difficult to track in both SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is beyond the SW limb. Opening field lines and rising filamentary material can been seen over the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning as early as 2026-07-19T19:30Z. There may be two distinct portions of the ejecta creating two features in coronagraphs; however, the greater leading edge appears to move together, so this has been treated as a single event. The eruption can be seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 from former AR 14482 (S09W121) beginning around 2026-07-19T20:15Z due to the instrument cadence.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 only. The leading edge is too faint/diffuse to track in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint, narrow, jet-like CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-19T23:00Z. It is also seen for early frames in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No good source candidate has been found on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of triangulation and lack of source candidate.

data.note: Wide CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is an eruption seen beyond the SW limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195/304, best seen as opening field lines starting around 2206-07-20T01:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is likely beyond the west limb as seen from SDO AIA and STEREO A EUV imagery. The source may potentially be seen as faint moving field lines near the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery starting at 2026-07-20T04:05Z. A filament eruption centered around S15W10 as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery starting at 2026-07-20T04:39Z was determined to not likely be the candidate source for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery as well as the potential source location.

data.note: CME visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a downlink data gap. The source is likely an eruption seen around S10W130 in STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery starting at 2026-07-20T09:15Z with brightening, an ejecta of material, and post eruptive arcades. Former AR 14482, which rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2026-07-17, may be the potential source of this eruption based on EUV imagery. Moving field lines are also seen beyond the west limb in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location as well as the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely a C1.6 flare as seen in SDO AIA 131 and an eruption starting at 2026-07-20T12:08Z with brightening and an ejecta of material best seen in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. This flare and eruption is associated with AR 14492 (approximately N15E65).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the source location.

data.note: CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SSW in STEREO A COR2. The source is an eruption with a broad region of dimming best seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery extending from S30W80 to N15W100 starting at 2026-07-20T12:05Z. Moving/opening field lines are also seen in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA, SDO AIA 193, and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement with additional imagery based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1, STEREO A COR2, and SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. This measurement focuses on tracking the leading edge of the majority of the material of the CME.
Preliminary measurement using early frames of imagery based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2, GOES CCOR-1, and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT as well as the source location.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2, following bright CME: 2026-07-20T13:26Z. The source for this CME is not very clear in STEREO A EUV imagery, but may be a small moving of field lines seen in SDO AIA 171 over the SW limb starting around 2026-07-20T15:05Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. Not observed in SOHO LASCO C3 likely due to faintness and/or the pylon, and not in GOES CCOR-1 likely due to faintness. The source is likely former AR 14482 located approximately around S08W135, observed only in STEREO A EUVI 195 as brightening on the region and field line movement deflected northward starting around 2026-07-20T18:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Thin, faint CME observed to the NE in STEREO A COR2 only, likely due to the GOES CCOR-1 occulting disk and real-time SOHO LASCO C2/C3 downlink gap (but also may be blocked by its occulting disk). The source is likely AR 14493, associated with an M1.1 flare in SDO AIA 131 peaking at 2026-07-20T19:20Z, also observed as brightening and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193 and field line movement in STEREO A EUVI 195 near its east limb around 2026-07-20T19:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D analysis using the source longitude of E09 to approximate the measurement, as such parameters may vary slightly. Due to several poor quality running difference images, only 3 available frames are used for this analysis.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source for this CME is not clearly defined but supported by triangulation around N33E42. This may be observed an area of weak dimming centered around N15E35 starting around 2026-07-20T19:39Z in SDO AIA 193, following a from AR 14493 responsible for CME: 2026-07-20T19:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No clear source is observed for this CME, and is likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 plane-of-sky with the unseen, likely far-sided source, and no STEREO A COR2 to triangulate.

data.note: Very narrow (<10 degree half-width), jet-like CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-21T22:12Z. It is also faintly seen in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is possibly related to a small amount of ejecta seen over the NE limb in SDO AIA 304 around 2026-07-20T21:18Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of triangulation and beyond-limb source candidate.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only. No clear source candidate is observed in SDO AIA or GOES SUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: This is a SOHO LASCO C2/C3 plane-of-sky measurement.

data.note: CME first seen to the WNW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-21T06:23Z. It is also seen to the NW in SOH0 LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is largely obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There is a larger shock feature that appears as a halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is most likely wide opening field lines seen near the W limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning around 2026-07-21T05:55Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of brightest, densest part of the leading edge based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
Shock front triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-21T07:48Z. It also seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is a filament eruption in the NW quadrant of the Earth-facing disk best seen in GOES SUVI 304 approximately centered around N45W60. The filament can be seen lifting off the disk as early as 2026-07-21T05:00Z. The filament eruption is followed by a wide-spread area of dimming best seen in SDO AIA 195. This CME follows and partially overlaps with the back of large, far-sided CME: 2026-07-21T06:23Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 and visible, on-disk source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery, and is faint but may be seen to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source may be related to an eruption/brightening from Active Region 14493 (N10W05) starting around 2026-07-21T12:00Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. There is a coronal hole north and south of this eruption site which may account for deflection from the on-disk source location.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative measurement based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2 and a faint leading edge seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. It is unclear if the feature visible in SOHO LASCO imagery is outflow or the same event that is seen clearly in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Slow moving, possible streamer blowout CME to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 (before data gap), GOES CCOR-1, and to the S in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is currently not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 due to the on going expected data gap due to downlink schedule. The source may be associated with moving/opening field lines in the SW quadrant below a coronal hole and between the longitudes of roughly W20 to W45 and latitudes of roughly S40 to S50 as seen in SDO/AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-21T21:00Z. A dimming signature is also visible to the SW starting around 2026-07-22T01:28Z. There is an additional dimming and brightening starting around 2026-07-22T11:00Z further to the S in SDO/AIA 193. All of these dimming features are believed to be associated with the overall streamer blowout feature to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement using GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 frames. There is likely deflection within the field of view due to proximity of a coronal hole.

data.note: Very faint front first seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-23T06:36Z. It is also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SSE in STEREO A COR2. There is some movement and brightening along a filament channel that was centered around S10W00 best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-23T05:54Z. This would require some significant southward deflection, but that could be accounted for by the proximity to a coronal hole south of AR 14493.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. There is some degree of uncertainty in this measurement due to the faintness of the leading edge.

data.note: Faint, narrow (<10 degree half-width) CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-23T10:36Z. It is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. A possible source candidate is some very minor field line movement from beyond the SW limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 as early as 2026-07-23T08:27Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the E in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-23T15:38Z. The source is most likely related to a C2.7 flare from around S20E19. The flare and associated eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 131. Field line movement and a faint EUV wave can be seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption appears to be directed northward.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit of features seen in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C3.

data.note: Faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely a filament eruption visible beyond the NE limb in SDO/AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 304 and 284 starting around 2026-07-23T14:17Z. The source is also visible to the NW in STEREO A EUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: May be associated with AR 14491, numbered on 2026-07-16.
An increase above x-ray flux background levels is observed starting at 2026-07-20T19:08Z, but this is to the east of the brightening observed with the M1.1 flare.
Simultaneous flaring from S20E19 and an unnumbered AR on the E limb around N06.
